hero.title: Facebook Messenger video size limit
hero.lead: Messenger accepts videos up to 100 MB per file — a limit raised from 25 MB in April 2024, so older guides quoting 25 are out of date. There is no time limit of its own; 100 MB holds a couple of minutes of full-quality phone footage or half an hour at a small picture size.
qa.h2: Messenger video limits at a glance
qa.r3.v: No time limit — only the file size counts. A longer video simply has to be smaller per second, which the compressor below works out for you.
qa.after: The cap is on the file, not on the length or resolution, so the useful question is how much video fits in 100 MB — answered below from what this compressor actually produces.
tool.lead: Drop the video below. It is compressed to just under 100 MB on your own device — nothing is uploaded — at the best quality that size allows, and checked so the result never lands over the limit. If the clip is too long to fit at a watchable quality, you'll be offered the opening stretch that does fit.
fit.h2: How much video fits in 100 MB?
fit.lead: Plenty — 100 MB is roomy compared with email or Discord. These rows are what this compressor actually produces from a typical phone recording — full HD, 30 frames a second, with sound.
fit.caption: What 100 MB gives you at different video lengths
fit.r1.q: Full HD at the original quality — nothing is lost
fit.r2.q: Nearly full HD, still sharp on any screen
fit.r3.q: Reduced size — clear on a phone, a little soft on a TV
fit.r4.q: Small picture; watchable, blocky on a big screen
fit.after: Even an hour of footage fits in 100 MB at a small picture size, so length is rarely the problem on Messenger. For a long video at full quality, a link — Google Drive, iCloud or Dropbox — is the better route.
over.h2: Over the limit? Compress or link
over.p1: For anything under half an hour, compressing to 100 MB keeps the video playing inline in the chat at a quality that suits a phone screen. For a long recording where quality matters, share a link instead — Messenger previews Google Drive, YouTube and most video hosts.
over.p2: Everything on this page runs locally in your browser — your video never leaves your device, and there is no account or watermark. Not sure a clip will fit at a decent quality? The bitrate calculator tells you the picture size 100 MB supports for your video's exact length.
faq.q1: What is the video size limit on Facebook Messenger?
faq.a1: 100 MB per file, since April 2024. Before that it was 25 MB, which is the figure many older guides still show.
faq.q2: Is there a video length limit on Messenger?
faq.a2: No. Only the file size counts. A ten-minute video is fine under 100 MB — it just has to be somewhat smaller on screen to get there, as the table above shows.
faq.q3: Why does Messenger say my video is too large when it's under 100 MB?
faq.a3: Check the app is up to date — older versions still enforce 25 MB. Also note that Messenger counts the file you attach, so a video that is 100.5 MB fails; the compressor above lands under the limit, never on it.
faq.a4: Yes, videos sent in chat are recompressed for delivery. Compressing yourself first to just under the limit means you choose where the quality goes, and Messenger has less left to squeeze.
faq.q5: Is my video uploaded when I compress it here?
faq.a5: No. Compression runs in your browser on your own device — there is no server, no account and no watermark. The only place your video goes is where you post or send it yourself.
